summary: PRE-CLAIM intent lock (ttl=600, no heartbeat) expires under any agent running >10min — dedup guard silently absent for the remainder of the run

payload.spec: .claude/skills/dispatch-claim/CARD.md Phase B — task_claim(..., ttl=600) with no heartbeat and release-in-finally
payload.observed: architect run 2026-08-26T00:37Z-01:00Z lasted 1369909ms (~22m50s); task_release at return reported ok:true released:0 — lock already gone. Unguarded window ~12m50s.
payload.second_instance: agent-father same tick ran 669440ms (~11m10s), also exceeding 600s — released:1 only because the release raced just inside a re-claim window.
payload.mechanism: Identical shape to the already-FIXED S2/ILC resume-key defect (feedback_resume_key_ttl_expires_under_live_agent_inverting_dedup, resolved ecb825731) but on a DIFFERENT key namespace: that fix heartbeats task:<row-id>, it does not touch intent:<agent>:<key>. The PRE-CLAIM guard is the one CARD.md calls the hard gate.
payload.impact: A peer session running the same PRE-CLAIM would see the key free and spawn a duplicate of a still-live agent. The router-side harness notice (Background agent still running) is out-of-band and unavailable to a peer terminal.
payload.suggested_direction: Either heartbeat the intent key while the spawned agent is live, or raise ttl to exceed realistic agent runtime (architect/agent-father routinely 10-25min). Do NOT simply raise the constant without bounding it — the sibling fix showed an unbounded keepalive inverts the guard the other way; any bound must live outside the renewed lock.
